facts.statement: The study aimed to find out how the SARS-CoV-2 virus triggers sneezing, coughing, and pain.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Researchers used mice and human cells grown from stem cells to test if a specific virus enzyme directly turns on airway pain nerves.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: When the virus enzyme acted on the nerves, it caused sneezing, coughing, pain, and the release of a specific chemical signal.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study found that both the virus enzyme and a specific channel in the nerve cell were necessary for the sneeze reflex to happen.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Other coronaviruses that infect mice also caused sneezing in the animal subjects.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The sneezing caused by the other mouse coronavirus also required the same specific nerve channel.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Infecting the nerve cluster with the virus changed the genes the nerves expressed, specifically turning up the pathway that links the enzyme to the pain channel.
facts.subject: animals
